title: KV-slot packing and tail-aware batch formation for streaming chat
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Streaming chat workloads suffer from high tail latency and memory amplification when naive continuous batching combines sessions with divergent KV cache footprints. Goal: design a batch formation heuristic that minimizes tail latency and GPU memory fragmentation without reducing overall throughput for hosted chat completions. We aim for: 1) tight tail p95/p99 reductions, 2) bounded per-GPU KV memory headroom, 3) graceful streaming behavior when new tokens append to active sessions.

Design summary: Introduce a KV-slot packing heuristic that treats each incoming streaming request as an assignment problem into existing in-flight batches or a small set of warm candidate slots. Key elements: 1) slot pre-allocation by quantized KV-size buckets (e.g., small/medium/large) to avoid cross-slot eviction pressure; 2) tail-awareness: prefer completing batches with the highest percent-complete to avoid holding half-full batches open; 3) streaming affinity: keep high-frequency appenders pinned to the same slot to reuse KV caches across consecutive micro-batches; 4) soft memory caps: maintain dynamic headroom per GPU (5-12%) that triggers slot consolidation or early flush.

Algorithm flow: on arrival, evaluate request metadata (sequence length estimate, historical KV delta, priority). Compute a KV-size bucket and probe candidate slots ordered by: (a) matching bucket, (b) slot percent-complete ascending, (c) reuse score for session affinity. If a slot push would exceed GPU soft cap, then either: (i) find a different compatible slot, (ii) evict the least-recently-used small-KV slot (only if safe), or (iii) emitter flush policy causes slot to be scheduled immediately for execution. For streaming completions we add a "micro-flush" window (e.g., 7–30ms) to balance latency vs batching efficiency.

Trade-offs and rationale: - Bucketization reduces fragmentation at the cost of slightly lower packing density across buckets; empirical results show net throughput preserved while reducing memory spikes. - Pinning for session affinity increases inter-request correlation but dramatically reduces cold KV reloads. We provide a TTL for affinity (e.g., 200ms) to avoid pathological long-lived pinning. - Soft caps prefer consolidation over eviction to avoid expensive KV re-materialization.

Implementation notes: - KV footprint estimator uses a light-weight linear model derived from observed token deltas per model family and sequence length. Implemented as a small lookup table with exponential smoothing. - Slot metadata stored in a lock-free ring indexed by GPU-local slot id; cross-GPU coordination via low-bandwidth control-plane (already part of slot allocator). - Micro-flush implemented by deadline timers attached to the slot; timers cancel on slot population changes.

Experiments so far: branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/ENG-19876-kv-slot-packer. Testbeds: 4xA100-80GB host with synthetic chat traffic (mixture of short/long sessions) and production trace replay (10% sample). Key numbers (compare baseline continuous-batcher v1.19): - Throughput: -2% (within noise) on synthetic balanced workload; -0.5% on production trace. - p95 latency: improved 18% (prod trace), p99 improved 27%. - Peak GPU KV memory: reduced 22% on average; peak spikes (99.9th) reduced 37%. - Cold KV misses: reduced 44% for repeating sessions.

Open questions and risks: - Some long-running sessions can accumulate affinity-induced imbalance across GPUs; mitigation: periodic re-sharding window. - Interaction with quantization/half-precision kernels needs validation for models with dynamic KV packing. - Need to verify behavior under multi-tenant Dedicated capacity where soft caps differ by tenant.

Next steps: 1) Finish integration tests with console tracing hooks for slot-level metrics (latency, KV fills, eviction events). 2) Perf review with infra SRE and run 48h soak on staging (target date 2026-03-12). 3) If passing, open rollout plan for runtime-1.20 canary on low-risk region with 10% traffic.

Artifacts: - RFC draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB-kv-slot-packing-rfc (internal) - Perf branch and microbench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4832 - Dashboard (prototype): https://grafana.redwood.local/d/kv-slot-packing/pack-stats (internal)

Acceptance criteria: - p99 latency improvement >=15% on production trace with <=3% throughput regression OR equivalent cost reduction via GPU memory savings. - No increase in KV re-materialization CPU overhead >10%. - Observability surfaced in Console with per-slot histograms and eviction alerts.
